name: VA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+26 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Democratic territory
Overwhelming money gap: Beyer raised about $2.5M versus roughly $42K for the Republican nominee
Incumbent Don Beyer is running and was renominated without difficulty
Prediction markets price a Beyer win at roughly 97%
model.rationale: A D+26 Northern Virginia seat, a roughly 60-to-1 fundraising advantage for the incumbent, and market pricing near 97% for Beyer all point to an easy Democratic hold; the only real question is the size of the margin, not the winner.
model.watch: A heavily funded outside-spending intervention for the Republican nominee or sharply depressed Northern Virginia turnout would be needed to put the outcome in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Don Beyer, a Democrat first elected in 2014, defends a Northern Virginia seat drawn deep into Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 26 points toward his party. The Republican nominee, Tony Sabio, has raised about $42,000 and holds minimal cash on hand, while Beyer has raised roughly $2.5 million. Independent and Libertarian candidates are on the ballot but lack resources. Prediction markets price Beyer's re-election at about 97 percent.

No public general-election polling covers the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. Those signals all point the same direction: a comfortably Democratic district, a well-funded incumbent, and an underfunded challenger. The main residual uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile contest, which could shave a few points off the expected margin without changing the likely outcome.
